title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Chapter I of the May 1966 letter to Tate, 'La notion de cristal'. Setup from the previous page: S is a prescheme over R. C is the category of R-thickenings T of S, meaning closed immersions S→T defined by a locally nilpotent ideal; no divided powers are imposed, so C is in effect the infinitesimal site. An F-crystal is a cartesian section over C of a fibred category F → (Sch)/R. In modern terms, a crystal in quasi-coherent modules is a module E_T on each thickening T, with transition isomorphisms g^*E_T ≅ E_{T'} for each map g: T'→T in C.

§1.3 Functoriality.
(i) Change of base. If S→R'→R, then C_{S/R'} is a full subcategory of C_{S/R}. Restricting a crystal relative to R gives one relative to R'. So an absolute crystal (R = Spec Z) gives a relative crystal over every base.
(ii) Inverse image. Let f: S'→S be a morphism over R. Grothendieck builds a functor C'→C. To an object S'→T' he assigns the pushout T = S ⊔_{S'} T'. Its underlying space is |S| (since |T'| = |S'|) and its structure sheaf is O_T = O_S ×_{f_*O_{S'}} f_*O_{T'}. The map S→T is again a nilpotent thickening, and there is a canonical map T'→T. One then sets (f^*E)(T') := (T'→T)^* E(T). This makes F-crystals over variable S a fibred category over (Sch)/R. The variances in R and S combine into one variance in the pair (R,S).

§1.4 The value functor. 'Valeur en S' sends a crystal E to E_S, a quasi-coherent module on S. Grothendieck warns that this functor is not even faithful in general. So a crystal should not naively be thought of as a module M on S plus extra 'structure cristalline', except in cases where the functor is faithful (forward reference to 1.8).

§1.5 Example (finished on the next page). Take S = Spec k with k perfect, R = Spec Z, and W the Cohen ring: W(k) in characteristic p, k itself in characteristic 0. A handwritten addition requires k algebraic over Q in characteristic 0. Then C is equivalent to the category of local artinian W-algebras killed by a power of the maximal ideal with residue field k. This uses that W_n(k) is formally étale over Z/p^n for perfect k, and that k/Q is formally étale. Consequently:
- crystals of modules are p-adic projective systems (M_n) of W_n-modules;
- finitely presented crystals are finitely generated W-modules;
- the value functor is ⊗_W k, which is not faithful: multiplication by p on W becomes 0.

The purpose of all this is to set up crystals as coefficients for a de Rham / formal-group (Dieudonné-type) theory in characteristic p.
errors: The pushout construction is called 'évidente', but in general it needs hypotheses. One needs f_*O_{T'} to be quasi-coherent, e.g. f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, or f affine as in Ferrand's pinching theorem. Without this, O_S ×_{f_*O_{S'}} f_*O_{T'} need not define a scheme with S→T a nilpotent thickening. Locally on S the construction works under these finiteness assumptions. Later treatments (Dix exposés, Berthelot) instead define inverse image via morphisms of topoi or local liftings.

Phrasing quibble: the functor C'→C is not literally 'compatible avec les foncteurs oubli'. What is needed is a natural transformation T'→T between the forgetful functor on C' and the composite C'→C→(Sch).

The characteristic-0 case as typed (k itself as Cohen ring for an arbitrary field k) is false: the section k→A of a thickening exists but is not unique unless k/Q is formally étale. Grothendieck's handwritten correction, requiring k algebraic over Q, repairs this.

missed.claim: This page uses an explicit pushout ('somme amalgamée') of nilpotent thickenings to define inverse image of crystals. This is a concrete, site-level alternative to the topos-theoretic definition that later became standard. The general existence question was only settled later (Ferrand, 'Conducteur, descente et pincement', 2003). It is a minor historical detail, not a new result.
missed.quote: il y a une construction évidente de somme amalgamée dans la catégorie des préschémas, qui donne un T=S⊔_{S'}T'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Pinching and pushouts of thickenings are used in deformation theory (Schlessinger-type conditions, Artin–Rydh algebraicity criteria). Here Grothendieck already uses them in 1966 as the mechanism for crystal functoriality.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known founding letter on crystals, whose content was developed in Dix exposés and by Berthelot. The only slightly notable detail is the pushout-based definition of inverse image, which is routine and needs unstated hypotheses.
transcription_corrections: 'criataux' is a typo in the original typescript (for 'cristaux'), not a transcription error.
The struck-out word after 'un' in line 3 is an overstrike; the intended word is 'cristal'.
The handwritten insertion after 'k lui-même' reads: '; dans ce dernier cas, supposons k algébrique sur Q.'
The overstrike above 'parfait' appears to be a struck-out 'de' or similar, not part of the text.
